page: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd5 is a bare-metal dedicated server running on the AMD EPYC 9255 processor with x86_64 architecture. The system provides 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs clocked at 3.2 GHz, paired with 384 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, achieving an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a dedicated 960 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address. The server operates without dedicated GPU acceleration, relying entirely on CPU vector instructions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 for accelerated arithmetic.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier compute and single-thread capabilities. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved a single-core score of 2,742.0 and a multi-core score of 25,509.0, placing in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. It demonstrated exceptional throughput in code compilation via Clang (59,880.0) as well as compression workloads, registering 39.78 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. The stress-ng single-core test reached 3,629.78, reflecting high per-core execution speeds from the Zen-based architecture.

Memory and I/O metrics align with high-capacity memory-optimized workloads, supported by DDR5 bandwidth reaching 205.04 GB/sec on large uncached read blocks. PassMark database operations scored 31,562.63, while Redis SET operations sustained 84.77 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput peaked at 102.69 GB/sec. On CPU-bound machine learning tasks, the platform processed 4,961.16 prompt tokens per second on small 135M models, though performance throttles down to 162.3 tokens per second on 7B models due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform yields strong multi-threaded and memory-per-core density without hypervisor overhead, eliminating noisy-neighbor degradation. The primary tradeoff lies in local storage capacity, where the 960 GB NVMe volume offers moderate space relative to the massive 384 GB memory pool. Consequently, this server is suitable for high-throughput in-memory databases, large-scale software compilation pipelines, real-time data processing, and enterprise application hosting.
description: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd5 is a bare-metal server driven by a 24-core, 48-thread AMD EPYC 9255 processor operating at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 384 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory and a single 960 GB NVMe SSD, without hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the top tier for single-core tasks (Geekbench single-core 2,742.0) and multi-core compilation (Clang score of 59,880.0), alongside strong memory subsystem results such as 84.77 million Redis SET operations per second and 102.69 GB/sec in web serving throughput. Compute features include AVX-512 vector support and secure virtualization extensions. With 8 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance offers exceptional compute and memory density, making it well-suited for enterprise in-memory databases, continuous integration build clusters, and high-concurrency web serving infrastructure.
